title: Live PG serves an ephemeral empty cluster after WSL/Docker restart; real equity_os data unattached
description: Found 2026-10-23 during the end-to-end analysis. ledger export --stock APARINDS fails: relation eqos.reporting_entities does not exist. Live equity_os on 127.0.0.1:55432 has only the public schema, no eqos_meta.schema_migrations. PG container logs show initdb ran on 2026-10-22 at 02:59 and 03:23 UTC (WSL boot 03:22:25). Inside the container /var/lib/postgresql is a 16G 'none' filesystem (Docker Desktop VM), not /dev/sdf. Host /data/pgdata/equity-os/18/docker mtime is 2026-10-11 09:07 (the last real start). A read-only throwaway mount sees it on /dev/sdf, intact, with a stale postmaster.pid. Inference: at boot, Docker Desktop resolved the bind mount before the WSL distro path was available, and the image's entrypoint initdb'd an empty dir. The 2026-10-22 gate (4401 passed) ran on the ephemeral cluster, using test DBs only. Fix: restart the container so the mount re-resolves (the classifier denied this; needs the owner's go-ahead). Then verify schemas and migrations 0041, and add a loud guard so runtime and the gate refuse a cluster without eqos_meta (or with a data fs other than the host disk).
notes: 2026-10-23 update: the real-disk cluster ran 10-11 to 10-14 only. Container initdb'd ephemeral VM storage on 10-14 03:18, 10-15 14:36, 10-22 02:59 and 10-22 03:23, so all DB work from 10-14 on, including the 10-20 cutover, was lost on restart. The owner restarted the container 10-23 03:41: real disk attached, crash recovery OK. The real equity_os has no schemas; the roles are only equity_os, eqos_migrator and eqos_runtime. Recovery source: post-cutover backup B2 data/backups/equity_os/49743901ddca40169881ff5d09fff073 (database.dump plus captures, 10-20 13:06). Next: (1) db bootstrap (classifier-denied, owner to run); (2) db restore B2 into eqos_test_* to verify; (3) a Sol-reviewed procedure to restore B2 into live equity_os; (4) a guard so the compose entrypoint refuses to initdb when the bind-mount sentinel is absent, plus a runtime/gate preflight that the live schema is present.
close_reason: Recovered 2026-10-23. The owner restarted the container (real disk re-attached) and ran db bootstrap. B2 was restored into live equity_os via Sol-approved scratchpad/e2e/live_restore.py (3 rounds), all checks passing. Mount sentinel guard live (compose entrypoint). Fresh backup 7ac5a42b has counts, runs and captures equal to B2. Live-state preflight follows in eqos-px2.

title: Source classification defaults open: unknown source_id is classified first_party
description:
DEFECT IN EXISTING CODE. Independent of the Upstox work; found while reviewing it.

src/fundamentals/reconcile/agreement.py:43
  DERIVED_SOURCE_MARKERS = ("screener", "tijori")

classify_agreement marks a source DERIVED only if its source_id contains one of
those two substrings. Every other source_id falls through to FIRST_PARTY -- the
highest authority the system has, granted by string default.

VERIFIED LOCALLY: both 'upstox' and 'upstox-fundamentals' currently resolve to
first_party. Any future source added without editing this tuple does too.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW. Upstox fundamentals are the one source PROVEN
non-independent of Screener (see eqos-0j6 and eqos-rdb). If an Upstox value ever
reaches classify_agreement -- through a report consumer reconstructing an
Observation, a third module importing both lanes, or an orchestration change --
it is granted first-party authority automatically. The Upstox plan's 'barred
from voting' guard is an import scan, which does not prevent any of those paths.

Found by Codex GPT-5.6 Sol during critique of docs/research/upstox-integration-plan.md,
2026-09-03. Citation verified against the code by the orchestrator.

NOTE ON A RELATED CORRECTION: the Upstox plan previously justified its bar by
claiming a leak would create 'a false 2-vs-1 majority'. That mechanism is wrong
-- derived sources corroborate but never satisfy the two-first-party count, so
Screener does not vote today. The real hazard is the opposite: Upstox would be
classified first_party, not derived. The plan has been corrected.

FIX
1. Fail closed: an unrecognised source_id must not be classified first_party.
   Either an explicit registry, or a required SourceClass on the source itself.
2. Add a typed EvidenceRole with a DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY member, rejected at every
   reconciliation entry point.

TESTS
  test_unknown_source_id_fails_closed_rather_than_defaulting_to_first_party
  test_reconciliation_entry_points_reject_a_diagnostic_only_evidence_role
  test_upstox_source_ids_are_never_classified_first_party

BLOCKS eqos-0j6 (Upstox Lane B). Lane B must not be built while the
reconciliation boundary defaults open.
close_reason: Fixed in 1fa9bd0. classify_source now resolves from explicit declarations in contracts/source_catalog.py; an undeclared source_id raises UnknownSourceError instead of defaulting to first_party. Verified: 'upstox' and 'upstox-fundamentals' are REFUSED, not first_party. EvidenceRole.DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY added and rejected at the reconciliation boundary (DiagnosticSourceError) -- the typed bar eqos-0j6 needs. All three entry points (goal_runner.reconcile_stock, report_builder, comparatives) resolve a catalog via stock_catalog(). Provenance was NOT given a source_class field: 68 construction sites, and it would not have worked because three ids come from YAML and one is built per filing. The class travels with the declaration instead. Tests: 1271 passed / 7 skipped in tests/fundamentals; ruff + mypy --strict clean. The 6 pre-existing failures under tests/equity_os_blueprint are eqos-xa1.

title: [Ledger] Recorder cannot parse the verdict artifacts reviewers actually produce
description:
Integration defect found on first live use (2026-08-15).

record_inventory_review.py parses artifact fields with ARTIFACT_FIELD_RE = ^([a-z0-9_]+):[ \t]*(\S.*?)[ \t]*$ — bare 'key: value' lines. All 324 verdict artifacts produced so far record those fields in Markdown TABLES (| `component_id` | `AUTH-REG-001` |), following design r2 §2.2's stated format precedent (the program-level inventory artifacts). Result: 0 of 324 artifacts parse; --dry-run aborts.

Second, harder gap: 'captured_at' is present in 0 of 324 artifacts. r2 §2.2 lists captured_at as a field of the evidence_refs OBJECT (UTC, <= review timestamp), but the recorder demands it as an ARTIFACT field. The design never says the reviewer must write it, so no reviewer did.

Why neither review caught it: the build review exercised the recorder against artifacts the BUILDER wrote in the builder's own format; the design reviews checked §2.2's content list but not a machine-readable contract, which §2.2 never states.

Fix direction (decide in design r3, do NOT rewrite evidence artifacts): amend the recorder to parse the documented artifact format, and specify captured_at's provenance. Modifying 447 review-evidence files to suit the tool is the wrong direction — the tool is ours, the evidence is the record.
acceptance_criteria: Design r3 specifies the exact machine-readable artifact contract incl. captured_at provenance; recorder parses the real artifact format; independent review CLEAN; batch 1 dry-run then real record succeeds against the canonical ledger with structural 0 before/after.

WHY THE EARLIER KILL INVERTS. The independence test (eqos-rdb step 1) found
Upstox shares lineage with Screener: operating_profit is Screener
profit-before-tax (12/12 across TITAN/HFCL/NETWEB, both bases), and Upstox
reproduces Screener divergence from the BSE filing on TITAN Jun-2026 net profit
(1777 vs filed 1699.00). That disqualifies these endpoints from adjudicating
truth. It makes them usable for detecting extraction drift.

CLAIM CORRECTED. An earlier version of this bead said a disagreement 'isolates
to one cause -- our HTML parse read the page wrong'. That does not follow and is
withdrawn. A disagreement means only that two representations differ. Other
causes: refresh/restatement timing (Upstox has no as-of field, rolling 4-period
window), different aggregation or formula, precision/rounding, an Upstox-side
defect, comparator misalignment, or Screener correctly rendering a vendor error.
Lane B gives a triage DIRECTION, not a diagnosis.

SCOPE
  A = log-only (owner). Never votes, never enters FactStore or reconciliation.
  B = all surfaces fetched (owner): income-statement, balance-sheet, cash-flow,
      key-ratios, plus a comparator over share-holdings from Lane A.
      profile and competitors stay excluded (no Screener counterpart).
  C = REOPENED. Awaiting the owner. See below.

DECISION C IS REOPENED -- ORCHESTRATOR ERROR. C was chosen as 'exact equality'
on an orchestrator claim of '12/12 exact'. That claim was false and the
contradicting evidence was in our own probe file. independence-test.md:56 says
'to the crore, OR WITHIN 1 CR ROUNDING', and Upstox returns decimals where
Screener displays integers:
    HFCL   Jun-2026  Screener PBT 332  Upstox 331.52
    HFCL   Sep-2025  Screener PBT 106  Upstox 106.34
    NETWEB Mar-2026  Screener PBT  95  Upstox  94.82
Exact equality is unachievable for these companies and would report ~100%
mismatch. TITAN's values happen to be whole, which made the sample look exact.

Also false: the plan claimed revenue would differ by at most 1 cr from compound
rounding. independence-test.md:63 records TITAN Dec-2025 Screener 25,415 vs
Upstox 25,567 (152 cr) and Mar-2026 51 cr. The revenue = Sales + Other Income
mapping is approximate, not exact.

PROPOSED REPLACEMENT: evidence-tiered outcomes, not one global threshold. Use
the repo's existing verify/crossfoot.observation_half_ulp and
verify/comparison_key rather than invent a tolerance.
  Tier 1 (equivalence demonstrated): income-statement PBT, PAT -> half-ULP on
         declared precision; difference = MISMATCH.
  Tier 2 (related, not equivalent): income-statement revenue, balance sheet ->
         interval arithmetic over rounded addends; difference = ANOMALY.
  Tier 3 (equivalence unproven): cash flow, key ratios, share holdings ->
         recorded and compared, never adjudicated; difference = NOT_COMPARABLE.
Cash-flow lineage was never tested. Balance-sheet evidence is weak. Ratios are
derived, point-in-time and formula-dependent. Shareholding buckets may be
defined differently.

GRADUATION IS NOT A BARE RATE. A disagreement rate cannot separate a parser
defect from timing drift, a bad mapping, a formula difference, a precision
artefact, or a comparator bug; and a low rate does not prove sensitivity.
  a. Hand-label a stratified sample against the retained Screener HTML.
  b. Seed parser mutations / replay historical parser defects to measure
     detection sensitivity.
  c. Choose warn/block per field and per root-cause class, not per endpoint.
Named review owner and deadline required, or log-only becomes permanent
unactioned telemetry.

title: Upstox API pilot: token-gated independence test + price/instrument lane
description:
The blocking prerequisite is now MET: PavanMV confirmed 2026-09-03 that the Upstox API access is ready (Developer App + Analytics Token exist). Research is complete and citation-audited -- docs/research/upstox-api-evaluation.md (2026-08-24, GPT-5.6 Luna research -> Opus 5 adversarial citation audit, all 16 load-bearing citations verified, zero hallucinated endpoints). Verdict: PILOT-FIRST, price lane leading.

Execute the pilot plan from that doc, steps 1-4 (step 0 is now done):

1. INDEPENDENCE TEST (decisive, do first). 10 ISINs: 3 large, 3 mid, 2 with known restatements, 1 dual-listed, 1 recent IPO. Three-way compare Upstox vs XBRL vs Screener/Tijori on statements. KILL CRITERION: identical-digit agreement with Screener's known errors == shared upstream lineage, not corroboration -> drop the fundamentals lane entirely. Upstox publishes no data-vendor attribution, so independence must be TESTED, not assumed. Feeding a non-independent third source into a fail-closed reconciler injects false confidence -- this is the whole risk.
2. DEPTH/SHAPE. Count actual periods returned (staff-confirmed limit is 4). Probe the undocumented time_period=quarterly on balance sheet + cash flow. Record INR-crore rounding precision to size the reconciliation tolerance against our rupee-exact XBRL.
3. PRICE SMOKE. Candles across a known split AND a known bonus -- split/bonus adjustment behaviour is UNDOCUMENTED and must not be trusted until observed. Then a deep pull 2000->today.
4. INSTRUMENT MASTER. Daily ~6AM IST JSON, NSE+BSE, carries isin/instrument_key/trading_symbol/instrument_type plus a separate suspended-instruments file. Join to watchlist by ISIN in BOTH directions and measure misses.

DECISION RULE: steps 3+4 pass -> adopt the price/instrument/corporate-actions lane (snapshot raw + content-hash, private use only). Step 1 proves independence -> additionally admit fundamentals as a 4-period annual cross-check with an explicit crore tolerance. Step 1 fails -> price lane only; record why in the research doc.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: Upstox does NOT replace scraping. Four periods of crore-rounded annuals cannot validate the depth Screener/Tijori provide. XBRL stays source of record.

TERMS: website ToU broadly prohibit storing/redistribution; an Upstox staff forum answer (2026-06-25) explicitly permits caching/storing responses for internal application use with no attribution required -- informal, not a contract. Safe envelope: private internal research, no public display, no redistribution. Written confirmation from Upstox is worth requesting.

SECRETS: the Analytics Token is a credential. Store it in ~/.secrets/ mode 0600, value-only, read via $(cat ...) or Path.read_text() inside scripts. Never in the repo, never in logs, never pasted into chat, never sent to a third-party model CLI.

RELATED: the instrument master directly solves bead eqos-6v2 (populate authoritative ISINs in watchlist.yaml) and additionally gives delisting/suspension detection we lack entirely today. Corporate actions cross-check feeds Phase 3 reconciliation (eqos-kx4.4).
notes:

Independence test COMPLETE, 2026-09-03 — kill criterion FIRED.

VERDICT: Upstox fundamentals SHARE LINEAGE with Screener. The fundamentals lane is dropped per the plan's own decision rule.

Evidence (orchestrator-verified against our own captures, not taken on subagent report):
1. MISLABEL FINGERPRINT (conclusive): Upstox income_statement.operating_profit is numerically identical to Screener's 'Profit before tax' row, NOT Screener's 'Operating Profit' row. TITAN consolidated Sep25/Dec25/Mar26/Jun26 = 1522/2223/1577/2429 in both, while Screener's actual Operating Profit is 1875/2713/1938/2890. Reproduced across HFCL (consolidated) and NETWEB (standalone): 12/12 points, zero exceptions. Two independent pipelines do not both derive identical PBT AND mislabel it identically.
2. SHARED ERROR: data/gold/TITAN-Jun-26.json already carried needs_human_review=True on net profit — BSE filing 1699.00 vs Screener 1777. Upstox returns 1777.0, matching Screener's divergence from the audited filing exactly.
   (Correction to the subagent's report: revenue is NOT an exact match — Screener 21356 vs Upstox 21502, a consistent ~0.6-0.7% gap across all four quarters. That line is a different derived definition, not a fingerprint. The subagent overstated it.)

CONSEQUENCES:
- The six statement/ratio fundamentals endpoints are REFUSED. Agreement between Upstox and Screener is one opinion counted twice; admitting both to a fail-closed reconciler would manufacture false confidence.
- operating_profit is actively WRONG as named — a consumer reading it as operating profit gets PBT. Reason enough to refuse regardless of lineage.
- 3-source reconciliation for fundamentals collapses to 2: XBRL (first party) + one derived opinion.
- CORE lanes UNAFFECTED: price history, instrument universe, suspensions, corporate actions, share holdings, FII/DII have no XBRL/Screener counterpart. Additive, not confirmatory.

ALSO SETTLED LIVE (steps 2-4 of the pilot plan):
- Candles ARE split/bonus adjusted (4 events, 3 ratios; largest drop near a 1:10 split was 5.0% vs the ~90% unadjusted would show). Implies Upstox restates history on corporate actions -> content-hash every fetch.
- Instrument master: 100% ISIN coverage on equity rows (22,433/22,433); instrument_key is literally SEGMENT|ISIN; 81/83 of our entity map hit with 0 symbol disagreements; all 9 ISIN-less entities resolved; both misses (ICICI Securities, Varanium Cloud) confirmed present in suspended-instrument.json.gz. Closes eqos-6v2.
- Account HAS Upstox Plus (expired-instruments returns 200) -> Backtesting available too.
- 4 periods everywhere, units_in=crore; time_period=quarterly works on income-statement ONLY (silently ignored on balance-sheet/cash-flow).
- competitors requires NSE_EQ|<isin> instrument_key, not a bare ISIN (400 UDAPI100011).
- Default Python-urllib UA is banned at Cloudflare (403 error 1010, not retryable) -> needs its own outcome type, distinct from RATE_LIMITED.
- to_date inclusive; rows most-recent-first; >10y daily request fails loudly with 400 UDAPI1148 rather than truncating.
- Postman collection is stale (2023-10-23, no fundamentals, no v3).

LIVE CAPTURE DONE 2026-09-03 (4 requests). The bead's premise is FALSIFIED: a real export surface exists.

POST /api/export/screen/?url_name=goto_sublist&sublist_id=1914148 -> 200, text/csv, 15215B, filename=core-watchlist.csv, 83 data rows. The replacement oracle is HTML-vs-CSV: 83 rows both sides, company-name sets exactly equal after HTML unescaping, no duplicates. Two server code paths sharing no parsing, so a cap or dropped row on either side breaks equality. Ordering differs (HTML user order, CSV alphabetical) so the join is on name, never position.

Seam shape: acquire BOTH artifacts in one run and cross-check. Neither is a superset - HTML has data-row-company-id, CSV has BSE/NSE/ISIN/Industry Group/Industry.

BIGGEST CORRECTION ACCEPTED (outer): this is NOT completeness. Two renderings agreeing proves consistency; both are fed by the same queryset (the export is parameterised by url_name, the page view's own name), so a shared cap or stale snapshot is invisible to both. The published guarantee is renamed throughout to CROSS-RENDER CONSISTENCY AT FETCH TIME, with completeness unproven above the largest observed list (83). SL4-22 is the tripwire: any pagination block or data-page-info element on the page forces INCOMPLETE.

DESIGN CHANGED BY A CAPTURE-CHECK (inner): the watchlist selector dropdown carries NO id - the selected entry is a plain <li> with a check icon, no href or data attribute. So 'enumerate the dropdown for the id' was ungrounded. SL4-17 now says: post the form action read VERBATIM from the fetched page (exactly one export form exists), never construct an export URL. watchlist_export_url is removed from the models.

OTHER ACCEPTED: EMPTY dropped from the outcome enum (unobserved, indistinguishable from a degraded page); scoped cookie jar rather than requiring a fresh Set-Cookie; catch Exception never BaseException; parse the media type so 'text/csv; charset=utf-8' passes; SL4-18 assert_logged_in (capture-checked: both Slice 0 markers present); SL4-19 trust boundary (retained HTML embeds a live csrf token; data/ is gitignored and untracked, and no log or artifact field may echo a token or Set-Cookie value); SL4-20 values parsed from the CSV, HTML comparison-only, published label is the CSV header; SL4-21 duplicate id/ISIN refusal.

The new test harness must pin the seam at the shared helper or at build_opener.

notes: Root cause (verified 2026-10-15): host clock oscillation, not code. title: [D3.4] Approval panel command and role gating of D1b queue commands
acceptance_criteria: `uv run pytest tests/fundamentals/test_ledger_panel.py` with a fake reviewer adapter: a reviewer `APPROVE` → `APPROVED`, its text, provider and model recorded as data; one success and one gate refusal with no reviewer call for each subject kind (report version, disposition proposal); the panel makes no decision on an interpretation. Refused by direct SQL: a panel verdict without its review, a review of another digest or subject, a review from another transaction, a reused review, a verdict that disagrees with the kind, and a panel decision on a subject whose chain holds an owner decision. A validation appended during the reviewer call refuses the review with no decision. Amounts: the reviewer output holds none; a panel `ACCEPT` of an `ACCEPTED_AS_DEFINITION` proposal records `explained_amount` equal to its pair outcome's absolute difference; a direct panel disposition without its same-transaction decision, with another kind or with another amount is refused. Direct SQL: two pairs of one result share run and key but differ in difference; binding the other pair's outcome to the item's proposal is refused. Owner precedence: an owner disposition, then a fresh proposal, then panel acceptance is refused; likewise after an owner decision on another proposal of the item; and in a two-transaction race, an uncommitted owner `REJECT` of proposal A blocks a panel decision on proposal B of the same item, which is refused once A commits. A panel proposal acceptance completes under a 5 s `lock_timeout` (its final gate reads the overlay inside the deciding transaction). Interpretations are owner-only: a panel decision on an interpretation is refused by the trigger (direct SQL) and by `review()` with no reviewer call, and an owner `ACCEPT` succeeds; an operand insert after the owner's decision is refused. The runtime role is refused on `compare queue dispose` and on interpretation decisions, and may `compare queue propose`. A blocking HIGH item added to the cited run's overlay appends a validation showing `MATCH_UNTRUSTED`, and the approval still binds its original validation. Verdict rules (unit).

title: verify.sh: the captured-identifier rail scans whole changed test FILES, not changed lines; a refactor slice cannot pass the gate
description:
Found 2026-09-04 on eqos-5db (cli.py split). Two gate defects, both orchestrator-facing:

1. RAIL FALSE POSITIVE ON PRE-EXISTING LINES. scripts/verify.sh step 5 harvests numeric identifiers from the private capture dirs and greps every CHANGED test file for them (verify.sh ~464-472). tests/fundamentals/test_comparatives.py has carried date(2023, 4, 1), a yoy/2023-10-01_2023-12-31/ fixture path and 'Q3FY24 2023-10-01..2023-12-31' since before the rail existed. Changing one import line in that file made the rail fire 'real captured identifier in a fixture: 2023' and route STOP, on lines the diff never touched. The diff-coverage check in the same script already computes changed LINES (changed_lines() at ~377); the rail should grep only the ADDED lines of the diff (git diff -U0 | grep '^+'), the way the paste rail intends. Until then any edit to a test file that predates the rail and mentions a year in a capture is un-gateable. Do NOT weaken the rail to exclude years; the 5(c) fixture that used 'Mar 2023' was correctly rejected.

2. NO REFACTOR ROUTE. gate escalates EXIT_CONTRACT when scratchpad/gate/<slice>-red.json is missing (verify.sh ~215), on the same branch that prints 'tests-untouched SKIP no red proof'. A pure refactor has no new behaviour to prove red, so ROUTE PASS is unreachable by construction; the only evidence the gate can give is its substantive lines (gate OK, skips OK, rails). Proposal: a 'refactor' mode (scripts/verify.sh gate --refactor <slice>) that requires the pytest pass count to EQUAL a recorded baseline instead of a red proof, and still runs every rail. Record the baseline the way red does, in scratchpad/gate/<slice>-baseline.json.

Evidence: scratchpad/gate/cli-split-*.log (gitignored). Same shape will recur on eqos-4ff (goal_runner split).
close_reason: Done 2026-09-05. (2) New 'scripts/verify.sh baseline <slice>' records the green test set; gate takes the refactor route when a baseline exists and no red proof: test-set equality on PASSED node ids, +1/-1 routes CONTRACT, both proofs present routes CONTRACT, unreadable baseline fails closed (found in orchestrator review: an empty comparison printed OK; fixed, stderr stays clean). description:

title: verify.sh: the red proof does not hash fixture modules, only files that yield node ids
description:
Found by the Phase 3 entity-map implementer, 2026-09-03. scripts/verify.sh mode_red hashes only the test files that produced collected node ids. A pytest fixture/helper module that defines no tests of its own (e.g. tests/fundamentals/entity_map_fixtures.py, 493 lines, and tests/fundamentals/screener_watchlist_fixtures.py before it) is therefore NOT covered by the tests-untouched seal.

Why it matters: fixture modules carry as much of the frozen contract as the assertions do. entity_map_fixtures.py computes ISO 6166 check digits, builds the synthetic records, and decides which fields are populated - an implementer who edited it could weaken or invert an acceptance test while the gate still reported 'tests-untouched OK'. The gate's own comment says the two-source path exists to close exactly this gap, so this is a known-shape hole rather than a design intent.

The implementer did not edit the fixture module; it reported that the gate would not have caught it if it had. Verified by the orchestrator against the proof file contents.

Fix direction: seal every file under the test paths that the acceptance targets import, not only those that yield node ids. Cheapest version: hash any tests/**/*.py imported (directly or transitively) by a sealed test module.

title: screener_screen: count-preserving membership churn is undetectable, and undocumented
description:
Raised INDEPENDENTLY by both sign-off reviewers (Sol xhigh and Fable 5.1 high), both PLAUSIBLE, neither a blocker. If one company leaves the screen before a page boundary and another enters after the current page, the stated total N and page count q are unchanged, serials stay continuous and ids stay unique - so the run publishes RESULTS with one row silently missing. Pure reordering across a boundary IS caught by the duplicate-id check; equal-cardinality churn is not.

No per-page oracle can close this. It is a property of walking a live paginated surface without a server-side snapshot token, and Screener exposes none that we have found. The inter-request spacing bounds the window, and fetched_at per page makes the window auditable.

Action is documentation, not code: state the guarantee honestly on ScreenArtifact or in the CLI docs - this seam guarantees ROW AND PAGE CARDINALITY against the source's own stated total at fetch time, not an atomic snapshot of set membership. A downstream consumer that needs atomicity needs a different mechanism.

title: screener_screen: a refusal does not record what the page claimed
description: From Fable 5.1 sign-off round 3, finding 3, CONFIRMED. When a walk refuses because the stated total changed mid-walk or the stated page is wrong, the refusal message carries no numbers and the refused page's stated_total/stated_pages are never recorded, because page metadata is appended only AFTER a page is admitted. So the success path is auditable from the artifact alone (SL3-23) but the failure path still needs re-parsing the retained bytes to answer 'how did it move'. Fix: put the observed and expected numbers in the refusal detail, and/or record the refused page's stated pair on ScreenFailure.

title: screener_screen: name the redacted-URL variables so the footgun is obvious
description:
In ScreenerSessionSource._fetch_bytes the parameter was renamed to source_url and a redacted local named url now shadows it, so every log line and error message structurally cannot carry the private screen query. The property is correct and verified live (a real screen still returns its rows), but the naming inverts the reader's expectation: url is the fake one and source_url is the real one. A future editor 'fixing' the inconsistency by passing url to urllib.request.Request would silently fetch query=[redacted] and get wrong data with no error.

Fix: keep url as the real one, name the redacted one safe_url or log_url, and add a comment saying why two exist. Behaviour must not change. Found during Slice 3 sign-off; not fixed then because it is latent, not active.

title: entity map: the S1 anchor uses JSON_ISLAND for a JSON artifact read from disk
description:
Ruling A26 (2026-09-03) moved the Screener-artifact anchor off CSV_RECORD, which was claiming a column_index against a JSON file that has no columns - a fabricated ordinal, the SL4-27 defect class. JSON_ISLAND was chosen because it addresses position honestly (island/table_key/row_label/column_label) and structurally BARS column_index, so no ordinal can be invented.

Residual, raised by the implementer: JSON_ISLAND's documented retrieval procedure is 'fetch a page and read the named json_script block', but this reads a published artifact JSON from disk. The anchor is now honest about POSITION (the actual defect) and still loose about PROCEDURE. A fully truthful fix is a JSON_DOCUMENT anchor kind; adding one was declined during the fix round to avoid widening scope mid-slice.

Cost of the fix: a new SourceAnchorType member forces a branch at three assert_never sites (store/fact_store.py, output/earnings_update.py, thesis/adapters.py) plus a _FOREIGN_ANCHOR_FIELDS row and a required-field branch in _check_anchor_consistency. Low risk, purely additive.

Also record here: EntityMap.lookup is ambiguous for namespaces where uniqueness is not enforced (SCREENER_SLUG, TIJORI_SLUG) - it returns whichever entity sorts first. Uniqueness holds for ISIN, NSE_SYMBOL, BSE_SCRIP and SCREENER_COMPANY_ID only. Recorded as a limitation in the lookup docstring under ruling A29; fix if a caller ever needs slug lookup to be authoritative.

title: screener_screen: replace the id()-based lxml proxy comparison and inline XPath
description:
Two MINORs from the Slice 3 implementation review (Opus 5 high), both real, neither urgent.

1. read_screen_pagination's containment check compares id() of lxml element proxies. It works and was confirmed working: pagination.xpath('.//a') runs first and its list keeps every proxy alive, so the nested lookup returns the same objects. But that is a consequence of retention order, not a documented lxml guarantee. If the two xpath calls were reordered or the list not held, the check silently goes False - which raises rather than truncates, so the failure direction is safe. Worth a comment at minimum.

2. The nested-options XPath is inlined and duplicates the contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' ... ') idiom that _TABLE/_PAGINATION/_OPTIONS hold as module constants; it differs from _OPTIONS only by ./ vs .//. Same for the 'limit'/'page'/'1' literals - coding-style.md forbids loose string literals.
